input: Get a skin cancer screening this summer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the user has seen a dermatologist before determines how much guidance they need to find the right type of provider and what to expect from the visit.
Knowing if this is just for themselves or also for family members changes the scope of scheduling and coordination required.
Insurance coverage or out-of-pocket budget affects which providers are accessible and whether a referral is needed first.
Whether they already have a dermatologist or primary care doctor to contact determines the immediate first action — booking an existing relationship vs. finding a new provider.
A general full-body screening is different from getting a specific mole or lesion evaluated; the urgency and type of appointment differ significantly.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like — just attending the appointment, getting results, or following up on findings — shapes how the task plan closes out.
A target timeframe within summer (e.g., before July vs. end of August) affects how urgently the user needs to act and how the deadline is set.

gold.taskTitle: Get a skin cancer screening this summer
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to schedule and complete a skin cancer screening appointment during the summer season.

questions.title: Have you had a skin cancer screening before?
questions.description: Determines whether the user is familiar with the process or needs guidance on what a dermatology screening involves.

questions.title: Is this screening just for you, or others too?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the plan needs to account for scheduling screenings for multiple people, such as a partner or children.

questions.title: Do you have insurance that covers dermatology visits?
questions.description: Determines whether cost or referral requirements are a barrier that needs to be addressed in the plan.

questions.title: Do you already have a dermatologist or doctor to call?
questions.description: Identifies whether the immediate next step is contacting an existing provider or researching and finding a new one.

questions.title: Is this a routine check or a specific spot concerns you?
questions.description: Distinguishes between a standard full-body screening and an urgent evaluation of a particular mole or lesion, which affects appointment type and urgency.

questions.title: What does completing this task look like to you?
questions.description: Clarifies whether success means just attending the appointment, receiving results, or completing any recommended follow-up care.

questions.title: When in the summer do you want this done by?
questions.description: Establishes a specific deadline within summer to calibrate urgency and set a booking target date.
